title: U.S. House · Mississippi's 4th District
area: South Mississippi, including the Gulf Coast, Hattiesburg, and the Pine Belt

context.text: Mike Ezell defeated Sawyer Walters in the March 10, 2026 Republican primary. Jeffrey Hulum III defeated Paul Blackman and D. Ryan Grover in the Democratic primary. Charles Claburn did not make the ballot for the American Independent Conservative Party.

summary.text: Mike Ezell has represented Mississippi's 4th Congressional District since 2023. A Gulf Coast native, he was a law enforcement officer for more than forty years, most recently as sheriff of Jackson County, before winning the seat in 2022 by defeating incumbent Steven Palazzo in a Republican primary runoff. He chairs the Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation subcommittee.

background.text: A native of the Mississippi Gulf Coast who lives in Pascagoula and graduated from Pascagoula High School in 1977.
Earned a bachelor's degree in criminal justice from the University of Southern Mississippi (1997).
Graduated from the Mississippi Law Enforcement Training Academy and the FBI National Academy, according to his official biography.
Worked in law enforcement for more than forty years, most recently as sheriff of Jackson County.
Placed second in the June 7, 2022 Republican primary for the 4th District behind incumbent Steven Palazzo, then won the June 28 runoff, 53.8% to 46.2%.
Won the November 8, 2022 general election with 73.3% of the vote, defeating Democrat Johnny DuPree and Libertarian Alden Johnson, and took office in 2023.

Serves on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, chairing its Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee, and on the Natural Resources Committee, where he is vice chairman of the Subcommittee on Water, Wildlife and Fisheries.
Won the March 10, 2026 Republican primary over Sawyer Walters, 84.1% to 15.9%.
According to his official biography, he and his wife, Suzette, live in Pascagoula and attend First Baptist Church of Pascagoula.

priorities.text: "It's time to fix the border crisis because border security is national security. As a member of the House Committee on Homeland Security, I'm fighting to secure our southern border and keep drugs out of our country."

"To protect our communities, we must stand up for law and order. As a member of the House Committee on Homeland Security, I'm fighting to ensure that law enforcement is able to do its job and keep criminals off the streets."

"As your Congressman, I'm working to cut wasteful spending, bring more high-paying jobs to America (and South Mississippi in particular), and lower the prices hard-working people pay for essentials like gas and groceries."

positions.summary: Cosponsor of the Life at Conception Act, which his office describes as codifying the right to life guaranteed by the Constitution.

record.text: Sponsor of the UPDATED USPS Act, which would target techniques used by drug smugglers to move fentanyl and other drugs through the U.S. mail.
Member of the House Committee on Homeland Security.
Member of the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.
Cosponsor of the Prohibition of Agricultural Land for the People's Republic of China Act, which would prevent China and its agents from buying American farmland.
Sponsor of House Resolution 63, which honored two Bay St. Louis, Mississippi police officers killed in the line of duty.

candidates.name: Jeffrey Hulum III
candidates.currentRole: Member, Mississippi House of Representatives, District 119 (since 2022)

summary.text: Jeffrey Hulum III is a Democrat and a member of the Mississippi House of Representatives for District 119, first elected in a 2022 special election. He is a retired U.S. Army sergeant major who served six combat deployments and founder of the nonprofit Extend A Hand, Help A Friend. He won the March 10, 2026 Democratic primary and cites the minimum wage, health care, and tariffs among his priorities.

background.text: Born in Gulfport, Mississippi; in his Ballotpedia survey he says he grew up in the Gaston Point community of West Gulfport.
Enlisted in the U.S. Army in 1996 and served 22 years, including six combat deployments to Kosovo, Iraq, and Afghanistan, retiring as a sergeant major; he says he received the Bronze Star.
Founded the nonprofit Extend A Hand, Help A Friend, which he says runs a mobile pantry, a free summer camp, and school-based food pantries and mentoring.
Won the July 19, 2022 special general election for Mississippi House District 119, 67.5% to 32.5% over Gary Fredericks, and assumed office August 5, 2022.
In the Mississippi House, was assigned in 2025-2026 to the Marine Resources (vice chairman), Ports, Harbors and Airports, Military Affairs, Tourism, and Gaming committees.
Won the March 10, 2026 Democratic primary for the 4th District with 57.7% of the vote over Paul Blackman and D. Ryan Grover.

priorities.text: "The Economy": says South Mississippi deserves an economy that works for working people, not just corporations and the wealthy.
priorities.quote: South Mississippi deserves an economy that works for working people, not just for corporations and the wealthy.

priorities.text: "Affordable Healthcare": says no family should go broke to see a doctor, citing rural hospital closures and rising costs in Mississippi.
"Quality Education": says every child deserves a quality education regardless of ZIP code.

positions.summary: Says in his Candidate Connection survey that he would vote to raise the federal minimum wage to $15 and index it to the cost of living.
positions.quote: In Congress I will vote to raise the federal minimum wage to $15 and index it to the cost of living

positions.summary: Says in his Candidate Connection survey that he would vote to bring home federal Medicaid dollars Mississippi has not accepted, make the ACA premium tax credits permanent and let Medicare negotiate prescription prices.
positions.quote: I will vote to bring home the federal Medicaid dollars Mississippi has turned away for over a decade, make the Affordable Care Act premium tax credits permanent to cut your premium, let Medicare negotiate the price of your prescriptions

positions.summary: Says in his Candidate Connection survey that, as a Mississippi state representative, he championed public schools in the fight against school choice.
positions.quote: I championed our public schools in the fight against school choice.

statements.quote: vote against tariffs that land on your grocery bill
cut the tax giveaway to the wealthiest before anyone touches your child's Head Start seat, your SNAP benefits, or your kids' summer meals

candidates.name: Carl Boyanton

summary.text: Carl Boyanton is an independent candidate for Mississippi's 4th District who lost primaries for the seat in 2020, 2022, and 2024. Born in Memphis, Tennessee, he founded Farmer Fresh Produce, LLC. He says he is running on term limits, reduced government spending, and ending party-line voting.

background.text: Born in Memphis, Tennessee, and earned a high school diploma from Bay High School.
Has worked as a warehouse laborer and founded Farmer Fresh Produce, LLC.
Ran in the Republican primary for the 4th District in 2020, losing to incumbent Steven Palazzo, and again in 2022, when he received 6.2% of the vote.
Ran for the seat again in 2024 and lost the primary.
According to his campaign materials, he supports term limits of twelve years in each chamber of Congress.

priorities.text: Says he wants to put "people over party," citing low approval ratings for both major parties.
priorities.quote: It is time to put people over party. Both parties have approval ratings under ten percent.

priorities.text: Says he will fight inflation and the cost of living by reining in federal government spending, citing the $40 trillion national debt.
Pledges to hold a town hall in every county every year if elected.

positions.summary: On his campaign website, says abortion should be prohibited in all but the most exceptional circumstances, with exceptions for the mother's health, rape and incest.
positions.quote: Abortion is not a form of healthcare or a casual choice—it is the ending of a human life, and as such, it should be prohibited in all but the most exceptional circumstances.

positions.summary: On his campaign website, says the U.S. should deport as many illegal entrants as possible, focusing on criminals, recent arrivals and those who refuse to assimilate.
positions.quote: We should deport as many illegal entrants as possible, focusing on criminals, recent arrivals, and those who refuse to assimilate.
